WebGPU first

Rendering

Abyssal uses a ReflectionLit path for mesh rendering, an HDR scene-color target with tone mapping, and specialized editor paths for grid, gizmos, and picking.

ReflectionLit

A lightweight material path with base color, metallic, roughness, emissive, alpha behavior, and one global environment reflection.

Material Assets

ReflectionLit values are stored in MaterialAssets and assigned to mesh nodes in Wings Assembler.

HDR Tone Mapping

ReflectionLit writes HDR color first. Bloom and tone mapping then compress brightness for display while preserving saturated emissive hue.

Editor Rendering

Grid, gizmos, picking, and overlays remain specialized and sharp instead of being tone-mapped with world materials.

Future PBR

The architecture keeps room for Unlit, StylizedLit, ReflectionLit, and full PBR paths later.

Current HDR Boundary

Bright emissive materials can exceed normal display range inside the renderer. Foundational bloom extracts sufficiently bright world surfaces, blurs them at reduced resolution, and combines the glow before tone mapping.

Common Mistake

Do not treat renderer-owned GPU state as asset data. Materials are CPU-side appearance assets; renderer caches own GPU buffers and bind groups.
